crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Retrieval-Grounded Legal Research
children.blurb: Retrieval-grounded legal research is the practice of answering a legal question by first pulling relevant authorities and documents from a defined corpus, then using a language model to summarize or draft from those sources with citations attached.

children.name: Adversarial Statutory Interpretation
children.blurb: Adversarial statutory interpretation is the practice of researching and arguing competing readings of a statute when parties have adverse legal interests.

children.name: Brief Drafting with Machine Assistance
children.blurb: Brief drafting with machine assistance covers the use of software to help produce legal briefs, motions, and memoranda for courts and clients.

children.name: Citation Auditing and Good Law Checking
children.blurb: Citation auditing and good law checking cover the verification of every authority cited in a brief, memo, opinion, or client advice, from case citations and pin cites to statutes, regulations, and secondary sources.

children.name: Jurisdictional Anomalies and Local Codes
children.blurb: Jurisdictional anomalies and local codes covers the places where AI rules do not line up: a state statute that conflicts with a city ordinance, a county procurement rule that reaches further than federal guidance, or a court rule that assumes a technology the local code never defines.

sections.body: Legal research and case strategy is the work of finding the law that governs a dispute, reading it closely, and building an argument that a court will accept. Artificial intelligence now performs parts of that work in practice, not just in theory. Retrieval systems search large collections of cases, statutes, and regulations to surface passages that match a query. Drafting tools generate first versions of memos, motions, and briefs based on those retrieved sources. Auditing tools check whether a cited case has been overruled, distinguished, or otherwise weakened. Adversarial reading tools help a lawyer see how a statute could be read against their client's position, and these are real functions in commercial legal software, though they operate under human supervision.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The state of the work is mixed. Retrieval is largely solved for common queries, but it still misses context and can return outdated or irrelevant material. Citation auditing catches many formal errors, such as a case that no longer exists or a citation with the wrong volume, yet it cannot reliably judge whether a case is still good law in a new jurisdiction. Adversarial statutory interpretation remains difficult because it depends on legislative history, agency guidance, and judicial doctrine that are not fully captured in text. Brief drafting produces fluent prose but can invent citations or misstate holdings, so every output needs verification. The site tracks 29 AI case law precedents, a small number that shows how young this area is, and the honest limits include the lack of guaranteed accuracy and the need for a licensed attorney to review all work.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages under this section fit together as a workflow. Retrieval-Grounded Legal Research is the starting point, where a reader learns how to build queries that pull relevant authority from large databases. Adversarial Statutory Interpretation then takes those sources and shows how to read a statute against a client's interest, looking for ambiguity and exceptions. Brief Drafting with Machine Assistance turns that analysis into a structured document, with attention to how much of the writing can be delegated to a model. Citation Auditing and Good Law Checking is the verification step, where a reader goes to confirm that every cited case is still valid and correctly quoted. Jurisdictional Anomalies and Local Codes addresses the problem of variation across states, counties, and municipalities, which is where many automated tools fail. A reader would go to each page for a specific task in the research and strategy process.
